title: Pilot Ops Credentialing and Benchmark Culmination
next_steps: Redwood to share dedicated capacity quote and adjusted SLAs
SE to upload 1k qps benchmark artifacts and raw logs to shared folder
Customer to provide IAM role ARNs and K8s namespace info for private pilot
Schedule follow-up deep dive on quantization impact (w/ bench results)
action_items: Evan Mitchell - send dedicated pricing + SLA doc - due 2025-02-03
Priya Nair - run 1k qps tail-latency benchmark and post results - due 2025-02-06
Tom Hsu - provide IAM roles, service account ARN, and K8s namespace - due 2025-02-02
Alison Reed - confirm retention window and share security checklist comments - due 2025-02-05
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-30 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes

Attendees:
- Evan Mitchell (Redwood, AE)
- Priya Nair (Redwood, SE)
- Karthik Rao (Redwood, CSM)
- Marta Alvarez (CedarBridge, Tech Lead)
- Tom Hsu (CedarBridge, SRE)
- Nina Park (CedarBridge, PM)
- Alison Reed (CedarBridge, Security)

Summary: quick checkpoint on credentialing and infra readiness for the pilot gateway; SE presented preliminary 500qps benchmark; agreement to run a 1k qps run and to finalize IAM/k8s creds so Redwood Private can be provisioned; security team requested retention and KMS detail.

[00:00] Evan Mitchell: alright, hey everyone thanks for joining, um, we'll kick off in a minute, looks like most folks are here. this is the weekly pilot checkpoint focused on credentials, environment gating, and the bench culmination that Priya ran yesterday.

[00:22] Marta Alvarez: hey Evan, thanks. quick ask, we need to make sure the private endpoint won't see any egress to public buckets; security is, like, pretty strict here.

[00:38] Priya Nair: totally, Marta. Priya from the SE team. for Redwood Private we deploy into your VPC, we can use a private subnet with no NAT and we support customer KMS for model keys. we'll show the network diagram first.

[01:05] Tom Hsu: yeah, that's the ask. also we need guidance on the service account and IAM roles for the k8s operator; don't want to overprivilege.

[01:22] Evan Mitchell: noted, Tom. Karthik, do you want to run through the credentials checklist?

[01:30] Karthik Rao: sure. so we sent the creds checklist in the shared drive — items pending: 1) IAM ARNs, 2) K8s namespace + RBAC manifest, 3) bastion host or private jump host if you want console access, and 4) SSO test user for admin role. once those are in we can spin up the private control plane.

[02:05] Nina Park: for timeline, if we provide IAM stuff by Monday, what's the earliest we can get the pilot running?

[02:18] Priya Nair: best-case, once we have the ARNs and the namespace we can provision infra in 48 hours, then we want to run the 1k qps benchmark which might take another day of tuning. so realistically about 4 business days.

[02:42] Marta Alvarez: ok, that aligns. can you remind us what priors you saw from the 500qps run yesterday? we saw some higher p95 on tail than expected.

[02:55] Priya Nair: yeah, good question. quick caveat — that 500qps test was on a mixed-sequence workload: 30% long-context tokens, so KV cache warmup impacted the first 60 seconds. the steady-state p95 was around 210ms for short requests and 420ms for long sequences. em... some of that is due to our batching policy — we intentionally keep batch windows small to meet latency SLO.

[03:35] Tom Hsu: is that with quantized weights? we want to understand memory and GPU utilization.

[03:42] Priya Nair: yes, that run used 4-bit quantization profile A — reduced memory by about 40% on the worker nodes. GPU utilization averaged 68% with spikes to 85% during longer context. CPU load on the host was low. we can provide the flamegraphs.

[04:05] Evan Mitchell: one quick note — when you run a 1k qps plan, we'll likely recommend enabling prefix cache for the first pass of the prompt library; that will shave tail latencies but you need to confirm content TTL.

[04:32] Alison Reed: retention is the big concern for security. what's the default TTL for prefix cache and logs?

[04:39] Priya Nair: default cache TTL is 24 hours but it's configurable; logs retention on the control plane in Redwood's hosted offering is 90 days for default, but for Private we can set retention to zero or stream logs to your SIEM — we integrate with customers' Kinesis/CloudWatch or syslog.

[05:10] Alison Reed: can you publish the SOC2 report and the KMS flow diagram? we need to review cryptographic flow with our auditors.

[05:18] Evan Mitchell: yes, we'll share the security pack and the KMS key usage diagrams — expect those in the shared folder after this call.

[05:35] Marta Alvarez: about failover — if a worker node fails during the 1k run, do you have automatic fallback to a compatible model variant? like lower precision or a smaller model to keep throughput?

[05:50] Priya Nair: we do. runtime supports automatic fallback rules — you can configure a policy: fall back to quantized variant or to a smaller architecture. we also have region fallback in the hosted mode; for Private you can provision a standby pool or enable cross-region replication if you want.

[06:18] Tom Hsu: curious — you mentioned the model catalog and verified profiles. can we pin a specific model version? we need deterministic outputs during the pilot.

[06:28] Evan Mitchell: yes, model pinning is supported — we pin by model hash and the deployment manifest ensures repeatable model artifact. rollouts are atomic and we can set canaries.

[06:45] Nina Park: can we get a table of expected token costs for each config? this helps procurement.

[06:52] Karthik Rao: we will include a cost breakdown in the pricing doc Evan will send — hosted vs dedicated vs private unit economics.

[07:05] Marta Alvarez: back to the bench, can you walk through the test harness? I want to make sure our prompts are represented.

[07:14] Priya Nair: sure — the harness is a simple HTTP client we run across worker nodes; it supports per-request sequence sampling, and we can replay your real prompt traces (anonymized) if you share them. we also support function-call style threads if your app uses tool calling.

[07:48] Tom Hsu: quick note, we'll only share anonymized traces; PII filter will run before we hand off anything.

[07:55] Priya Nair: perfect, send the link to the trace export and we'll ingest into the harness. for the 1k test we'll want a 30-minute sustained window to capture tail behavior.

[08:10] Evan Mitchell: ok, for instrumentation — Priya, can you describe the logs and metrics you'll push so SRE can correlate?

[08:18] Priya Nair: sure — we push per-token latencies, batch sizes, cache hit rates, KV cache sizes, GPU mem usage, and per-request model variant used. we can emit metrics to your prometheus endpoint or push logs to the bucket you designate.

[08:40] Nina Park: Tom, any blockers on your side for providing the ARNs?

[08:45] Tom Hsu: we have a policy review tomorrow; I think we can get them out Monday but I need to confirm with infra.

[09:00] Marta Alvarez: if Monday then provisioning mid-week sounds right. can Redwood do a dry run deployment into our staging first so we don't hit production quotas?

[09:12] Priya Nair: yes, we typically provision into staging first. we'll use a non-prod namespace and a scaled-down worker pool to validate connectivity; then scale to pilot configuration.

[09:30] Evan Mitchell: quick interruption — Nina, for success criteria, are we still tracking latency < 200ms p95 for short sequences and uptime 99.9%?

[09:40] Nina Park: yes, that's the ask from product. also cost per 1k tokens target is in the doc but we're flexible if latency holds.

[09:55] Priya Nair: if you want <200 p95 consistently we'll tune batching and keep the batch aggregation window at 5-7ms; that tends to keep the long-context tail under control for short requests.

[10:10] Tom Hsu: curious about autoscaling — will node spin up latency impact SLOs during startup?

[10:17] Priya Nair: autoscaling uses buffer pools and warm spare capacity; we can provision burst capacity so you don't see cold-starts. for Dedicated customers we pre-reserve GPUs so cold-starts are minimized.

[10:34] Marta Alvarez: any licensing implications for model variants? especially if you fall back to a smaller model.

[10:41] Evan Mitchell: good flag — the licensing depends on the model we deploy; we have curated open models with permissive licenses and we can advise. we'll document specific model license bullets in the proposal.

[11:00] Nina Park: can we pivot to the bench artifacts now? Priya, what did you observe in the worker logs for queuing behavior?

[11:10] Priya Nair: there was a small queuing spike during a 10s burst in minute 12 of the run — batch sizes jumped which is expected. we'll attach raw logs; the tail spike correlated with prior KV misses. after warmup the cache hit rate was 87% which is decent but if you pre-populate the cache for common prefixes we can push that to 95%.

[11:45] Tom Hsu: pre-populate sounds good. how would that work operationally? do you need a sidecar or do we push a manifest?

[11:53] Priya Nair: we accept a prefix manifest (JSON) and we can ingest via the control plane API or CLI. the runtime will fetch prefixes into KVC on init. we'll provide a small utility to generate the manifest from your trace.

[12:12] Marta Alvarez: sounds good. Alison, any security follow-ups?

[12:18] Alison Reed: yes — two items: 1) show the crypto-in-transit and at-rest diagrams, and 2) confirm that the private control plane doesn't store plaintext prompts — we need an assurance for our privacy policy.

[12:32] Priya Nair: control plane logs can be configured to redact prompt text; by default prompts are hashed in logs and full text is optional and can be disabled. we'll include those config toggles.

[12:50] Evan Mitchell: quick housekeeping — I'll upload the security pack and the pricing sheet after this call. Karthik will follow up on procurement questions.

[13:02] Karthik Rao: yep, procurement enablement: we'll include a sample SOW and a draft MSA to speed legal review.

[13:20] Nina Park: on the MSA, there's often a question about indemnity when models generate hallucinations. do you have a policy or recommended language?

[13:32] Evan Mitchell: we include a limited liability and an acceptable use clause; we can surface suggested language but legal typically still negotiates. we'll add a note in the docs for your counsel.

[13:50] Tom Hsu: for the run itself, Priya, will you coordinate the traffic generator? we can also run from our infra to better emulate real network conditions.

[13:59] Priya Nair: we can coordinate a joint run — we'll provide the harness and can run it from your VPC to capture network variance. recommend a synchronized start time so we get consistent traces.

[14:20] Marta Alvarez: ok. let's pick next Wed for the 1k run unless there are objections.

[14:27] Nina Park: next Wed works for product. Tom to confirm infra availability.

[14:35] Tom Hsu: will confirm by EOD Monday.

[14:40] Evan Mitchell: great. recap of commitments: Evan to send pricing + security pack; Priya to run 1k benchmark and upload logs; Tom to share ARNs; Alison to provide retention comments. we'll target the 1k run next Wed pending ARNs.

[15:00] Marta Alvarez: one more question — can Redwood support streaming responses with chunked token delivery? our UI leverages streaming heavily.

[15:10] Priya Nair: yes, streaming is supported; we support server-sent events and chunked HTTP. streaming is slightly more resource sensitive but it's enabled in our runtime; we can supply client SDK examples.

[15:30] Nina Park: also curious about function/tool calling — we have a suite of internal tools called "docfetch" that we want to call synchronously. any caveats?

[15:40] Priya Nair: function calling is supported; we recommend sandboxing tool execution and having a retry policy. we'll map the tool-calling latency into the end-to-end numbers so you can see impact.

[16:00] Evan Mitchell: all right, any final questions?

[16:05] Alison Reed: please include a short note about key rotation policy for KMS keys; auditors like that spelled out.

[16:12] Evan Mitchell: will do.

[16:20] Karthik Rao: i'll schedule the procurement kickoff once the pricing doc is live.

[16:35] Nina Park: thanks everybody, that was helpful.

[16:40] Evan Mitchell: thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts and action items. bye.

End of transcript.
